title: Systematic Debugging
description: Turn failures into small, testable hypotheses using tracebacks, inspection, logs, and breakpoints.
learning_objectives: Read tracebacks and inspect runtime state

sections.title: Core mental model
sections.markdown: Debugging starts with a reliable reproduction: record the input, environment, expected result, and actual result. Read a traceback from the final exception upward to the first frame owned by your code. The exception type explains the category, while the message and failing line narrow the immediate cause.

examples.explanation: A small executable example exposes the rule instead of only naming it.

sections.checkpoint: Explain the example one line at a time without using vague terms.

sections.title: Operations and trade-offs
sections.learning_objective: Read tracebacks and inspect runtime state
sections.markdown: Reduce the failure into minimal cases, then use hypothesis testing: form one falsifiable explanation and seek evidence against it. Inspect types, values, boundaries, and side effects. Use focused logging with context rather than scattered prints; use a breakpoint (`breakpoint()` or an IDE) to step through control flow and inspect state. Tests make the reproduction durable and prevent regression.

sections.checkpoint: What input or state would make this code fail?

sections.title: Worked practice
sections.learning_objective: Trace the concept on concrete data.
sections.markdown: Work from the input and state the invariant before coding. Change one variable at a time, predict what evidence would support the hypothesis, and record the result. If the hypothesis fails, discard it. Common mistakes are fixing the symptom before finding the cause, catching every exception, logging secrets, changing several things together, and assuming the most recent code caused the problem without checking version history. For an interview, narrate the observation, the rule you are applying, and the resulting value. That sequence makes reasoning inspectable and exposes hidden assumptions.

examples.explanation: Trace names and values after every important line, then compare with the expected output.

sections.title: Common mistakes and fixes
sections.learning_objective: Diagnose failures rather than memorize syntax.
sections.markdown: Change one variable at a time, predict what evidence would support the hypothesis, and record the result. If the hypothesis fails, discard it. Common mistakes are fixing the symptom before finding the cause, catching every exception, logging secrets, changing several things together, and assuming the most recent code caused the problem without checking version history. Turn each failure into a focused test. Preserve the original failing input, make the smallest correction, and run the test again. Avoid broad exception handling or a rewrite that hides the root cause.
sections.checkpoint: Name one tempting fix that would only hide the defect.

sections.title: Interview-focused summary
sections.markdown: A strong explanation starts with the mental model, demonstrates it using a short executable example, names the trade-off, and closes with a common failure mode. Apply that structure to Systematic Debugging. In Forge Arena, solve related Python problems without tutor help when you want the attempt to count as clean transfer evidence.
key_points: Explain the why, not only syntax.
Use Arena for independent transfer practice.
